messages:
Lena V: Short thread: we need to pick a final approach for edge policy evaluation boundary. two practical constraints: 1) sub-2ms median for hot paths, 2) single-button rollback for incidents. Thoughts?
Marco P: Lean hybrid. Keep trivial, deterministic rules local (region affinity, tier pins). Complex, tenant-scoped state (real-time budgets, overrides) stays central.
Hannah C: Agree. Add an explicit `execution` flag in policy metadata (local|central|hybrid). Compiler enforces signal availability.
Diego: Runtime safety: local must fail-safe. If a declared signal is missing or policy-version mismatch -> return PRESET_SAFE_ROUTE and emit `policy_fallback` with reason.
Lena V: We should also require a shadow period: local computes decisions but does not apply for 24-72h, collect divergence and cost-delta. Only after automated checks pass do we enable active local.
Marco P: Distribution: delta-push over control-plane websocket with seq numbers + compressed pull fallback. Sign blobs with KMS and include a checksum.
Hannah C: CI integration: simulate policy against historical traces. Lint rule: execution=local cannot reference central-only signals. Fail CI if divergence > threshold in sim.
Diego: Telemetry fields proposed: policy_id, policy_version, decision_source, matched_rule_id, decision_latency_ms, divergence_flag, estimated_cost_delta, fallback_reason. Make names stable.
ops-bot: Note 9: added `policy_divergence_rate` and `local_fallback_rate` panels to console; alerts set for divergence > 0.5% over 5m.
Lena V: OK, I'll draft a short RFC: execution metadata, compatibility checks, fallback contract, telemetry schema, rollout checklist (ci-sim -> central-canary -> local-shadow -> staged-active), delta-push proto sketch, ops endpoints. Ping for review.
